root_cause.text: The f2fs_finish_read_bio() function was performing sanity checks on folio data without first verifying that the I/O operation completed successfully, causing access to uninitialized folio content when a read error occurred.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (bio->bi_status == BLK_STS_OK &&` before calling `f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer()`. The CVE description explicitly states "we may access uninit data in folio if we failed to read the data from device into folio," and the fix prevents the sanity check from executing when `bio->bi_status` indicates an I/O error, ensuring that only successfully read data is validated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard condition to skip node footer sanity checks when the bio I/O operation has already failed.
intent_record.what: Added a new condition `bio->bi_status == BLK_STS_OK &&` at the beginning of the existing multi-part if statement that checks node inode and folio properties before calling f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer().
intent_record.how: The sanity check on the node footer is now only performed when the bio operation completed successfully (BLK_STS_OK status). Previously, the sanity check would execute regardless of whether the I/O operation had already failed. This prevents unnecessary sanity checks and potential false error reporting when the bio already has an error status.

This prevents access to uninitialized folio content by ensuring checks only occur after successful I/O completion, which is exactly what the vulnerability root cause describes as missing.
